pubmed.rcsb_pubmed_abstract_text: Oxytocin is a neuropeptide that binds copper ions in nature. The structure of oxytocin in interaction with Cu <sup>2+ </sup> was determined here by NMR, showing which atoms of the peptide are involved in binding. Paramagnetic relaxation enhancement NMR analyses indicated a binding mechanism where the amino terminus was required for binding and subsequently Tyr2, Ile3 and Gln4 bound in that order. The aromatic ring of Tyr2 formed a π-cation interaction with Cu <sup>2+ </sup>. Oxytocin copper complex structure revealed by paramagnetic relaxation enhancement NMR analyses.
